title: 2025 Supervisory Stress Test Methodology
summary: The Federal Reserve published its 2025 Supervisory Stress Test Methodology document detailing the models and frameworks used to assess capital adequacy of large banks ($100B+ in assets) under hypothetical severe recession scenarios. The methodology covers projections of pre-tax net income, loan losses across multiple asset categories (corporate, commercial real estate, residential mortgage, credit card), and regulatory capital ratio calculations.
key_points: Supervisory stress test applies to bank holding companies (BHCs), covered savings and loan holding companies (SLHCs), and intermediate holding companies of foreign banking organizations (IHCs) with $100 billion or more in assets
The Federal Reserve conducts stress tests annually as required by the Dodd-Frank Act to ensure large banks remain sufficiently capitalized during severe recessions
The methodology includes models for projecting pre-provision net revenue, loan losses, and other losses across corporate, CRE, residential mortgage, and credit card loan portfolios
Stress test cycle publishes four documents: Stress Test Scenarios (mid-February), Methodology (June), Results (end of Q2), and Large Bank Capital Requirements (Q3)
Modeled loss rates cover five asset categories: corporate loans, commercial real estate loans, first-lien residential mortgages, domestic credit cards, and other loan categories
Results inform individual capital requirements for participating banks under the regulatory framework (12 C.F.R. pt. 238, subpt. O; pt. 252, subpt. E)
why_it_matters: This methodology document defines how the Federal Reserve models bank performance under adverse economic conditions. While it does not directly move markets, the stress test results published later in the cycle directly affect capital requirements for major banks, influencing their capacity to lend and potentially affecting credit availability. Market participants monitor these results to assess potential tightening of bank balance sheets.
